guide.summary: Box supports standard OAuth 2.0 for user-facing apps, and Composio has a managed Box OAuth app, so prototyping needs no setup of your own. Creating your own app is quick. Unlike server-side (JWT or Client Credentials) apps, an OAuth 2.0 app does not need admin authorization by default; a customer's Box Admin only has to enable it if their enterprise keeps unpublished apps inactive. Box publishes no timeline for the optional Integrations listing review.

composio.note: Composio lists Box under Composio-managed OAuth. No Box-specific credential guide was found in the dossier. See https://docs.composio.dev/toolkits/managed-auth for managed vs custom auth.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype on your own Box account: Composio's managed app works. Bring your own Box app for production with your own branding, scopes or quota, or when many customer enterprises will connect.
reasons: Your own app name and branding on the consent screen (the managed app is shared)
Control over the scopes and access level configured on the app
Your own quota rather than a shared app's
Distribution to many customer enterprises, each of whose admins must authorize your Client ID
Optional Box Integrations listing, which requires your own OAuth 2.0 app

scenarios.label: Prototype on your own Box account
scenarios.when_this_applies: You test with your own free developer (Individual) account, or just use Composio's managed app.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured. Free developer apps are authorized automatically (c3).

scenarios.label: Internal tool in your company's Box enterprise
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your own app runs against your employer's Box enterprise and you are not a Box Admin.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured.

waiting.estimate: None, unless your admin must enable the app
waiting.basis: OAuth 2.0 apps need enablement only where unpublished apps are inactive by default (c12).

scenarios.approval: Usually none for an OAuth 2.0 app. A Box Admin or Co-Admin enables it only if your enterprise keeps unpublished apps inactive by default.

scenarios.label: Multi-customer B2B product
scenarios.when_this_applies: Customers from different enterprises connect their Box accounts to your product, with no marketplace listing.

hands_on.estimate: 1-3 hours for setup, plus ongoing onboarding support
hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured.

waiting.basis: Each customer's admin must approve, and the timing is theirs (c4, c9).

scenarios.approval: No global Box review. Each customer enterprise's admin may need to enable your app if unpublished apps are inactive there.

scenarios.label: Public Box Integrations listing
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want to be listed in Box Integrations so other enterprises can discover the app.

hands_on.basis: Checklist, assets and descriptions are required (c6), but no time basis exists.

waiting.basis: Docs say only that the Box Partner team reviews 'as soon as possible'. No SLA is published (c6).

scenarios.approval: Box Partner team review of the Integrations submission.

prerequisites.title: Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: A free developer (Individual) account or an enterprise account with access to the Developer Console.

prerequisites.title: Composio account and dashboard access
prerequisites.detail: Needed to create an auth config and copy its redirect/callback URI.

prerequisites.title: Box Admin contact (enterprise scenarios)
prerequisites.detail: Someone who can authorize your Client ID in Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps. If you don't know your admin, check the Admin Contact at the bottom of your Box Account Settings page.

prerequisites.title: Listing assets (only for the Integrations listing)
prerequisites.detail: Categories, short and long descriptions, Add button URL, screenshots and an app icon. The app must be production-ready and use OAuth 2.0.

steps.title: Decide whether managed OAuth is enough
steps.detail: For a prototype, use Composio's managed Box app and skip the rest. For production with your own branding, scopes or many customers, continue.
steps.done_when: You've chosen managed or your own app.

steps.title: Create a Box Platform App of type User (OAuth 2.0)
steps.detail: In the Box Developer Console, create a Platform App and choose the User app type. Server types (JWT/CCG) are not end-user consent flows.
steps.done_when: The app exists and its Configuration tab shows a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your own credentials and copy the callback URI
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, create a Box auth config using your own client ID and secret. Copy the redirect/callback URI that Composio shows. Do not hard-code one.
steps.done_when: The auth config is saved and you have the callback URI copied.

steps.title: Register the Composio redirect URI in the Box app
steps.detail: Paste the copied callback URI into the redirect URI setting on the Box app's Configuration tab and set the scopes you need. An agent can check the pasted URI matches exactly.
steps.done_when: The Box app lists the Composio URI as a redirect URI.

steps.title: If needed, have a Box Admin enable the app
steps.detail: Only if the enterprise keeps unpublished apps inactive by default: send the Client ID to a Box Admin, who enables it under Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps. Customers' admins do the same for their enterprise.
steps.done_when: The admin has approved and you get the approval email.

steps.title: Wait for the admin, if enablement was needed
steps.detail: Timing depends on the admin; Box publishes none. Re-authorization is needed whenever scopes or access level change.
steps.done_when: The app shows as authorized or enabled.

steps.title: Connect a test account through Composio
steps.detail: Run the Composio connect flow for a Box user and complete the consent screen. Each end user must consent for their own connected account.
steps.done_when: A connected account is active and a Box tool call succeeds.

steps.title: Prepare listing materials
steps.detail: An agent can draft the descriptions, check the submission checklist items and list the required assets.
steps.done_when: Drafts are ready for you to review.

steps.title: Submit for approval in the Publishing tab
steps.detail: Confirm the checklist, fill in the form, preview, and click Submit for Approval. Questions go to integrate@box.com.

steps.title: Wait for Box Partner review
steps.done_when: The app is approved or Box asks for changes.

traps.title: Server auth types are not the right choice here
traps.detail: JWT and Client Credentials Grant apps are server-side, not end-user consent flows. For Composio user connections choose the User (OAuth 2.0) type.

traps.title: Scope changes force re-authorization
traps.detail: Enterprise developers must resubmit to the admin after changing scopes or access level, otherwise the changes don't take effect.

traps.title: Some customer admins must enable your app
traps.detail: Enterprises that keep unpublished apps inactive by default need their own admin to enable your Client ID. Ask about this during customer onboarding.

traps.title: Listing requires OAuth 2.0 only
traps.detail: Integrations do not support any other authentication methods.

blockers.symptom: Configuration tab shows 'Submit app for authorization'
blockers.what_it_means: You are not a Box Admin or Co-Admin, so an admin must approve the app.
blockers.what_to_do: Select Submit. Your admin gets an email, and you get an email on approval or denial.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft a message to the admin with the Client ID, scopes and purpose.

blockers.symptom: Users in a customer's enterprise can't use the app
blockers.what_it_means: That enterprise's admin hasn't authorized your Client ID yet.
blockers.what_to_do: Send the customer admin your Client ID and the steps under Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps.

blockers.what_it_means: The app needs re-authorization after scope or access level changes.
blockers.what_to_do: Resubmit to the admin, or have the admin choose Reauthorize in the Platform Apps tab.

open_questions: Box Integrations review time: not published. Ask integrate@box.com.
Admin approval time: depends on each admin, with no published figure.
Whether Box charges for listing or partner tiers: not found in the docs read.
Whether unpublished user-auth apps in free developer accounts have a user cap: not found in the docs read.
The exact scope list was not enumerated from the pages read; check the app's Configuration tab.
The probe of the authorize endpoint did not show how Box rejects invalid client IDs, so no rejection behavior is claimed.
